# Erdős Problem 31

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/31](https://www.erdosproblems.com/31)
- [Er56] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in additive number theory*. Colloque sur la Théorie des
  Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 127-137.
- [Er59] Erdős, P., *Über einige Probleme der additiven Zahlentheorie*. Sammelband zu Ehren des 250.
  Geburtstages Leonhard Eulers (1959), 116-119.
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial
  theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.

  (1954), 838-841.
-/

namespace Erdos31

open Filter
open scoped Pointwise

/--
Given any infinite set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ there is a set $B$ of density $0$ such that $A+B$ contains all except finitely many integers.

Conjectured by Erdős and Straus. Proved by Lorentz [Lo54].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos31.lean"]
theorem erdos_31 : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite →
    ∃ B : Set ℕ, B.HasDensity 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ A + B := by
  sorry

end Erdos31

reformulations.difference: The source says that A+B contains all except finitely many natural numbers; Lean expresses this as eventual membership along atTop.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On ℕ, Nat.cofinite_eq_atTop identifies atTop with the cofinite filter. Consequently, (∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ A+B) is equivalent to (A+B)ᶜ.Finite, and also to ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, a+b=n. Both equivalences were proved in the scratch file without using the admitted problem theorem.

review.notes: Checked the sole declaration and all cited papers’ relevant passages. HasDensity defaults to density relative to all of ℕ and uses real division; its ncard arguments are finite initial segments. The denominator-zero case occurs only at N=0 and does not affect the limit. Empty and singleton A are excluded by infinitude; an empty B cannot satisfy eventual coverage. Boundary tests and statement-equivalence proofs compile in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the named equivalences have no sorryAx dependency. The solved category and external Lean-proof record agree with the current source. The linked proof’s final statement was inspected, not independently rebuilt.
